questions: Which properties of states, paths or genealogies are required by specified continuation criteria?
What follows when transformation rules, criteria or representations become objects of transformation?
Which states and targets remain reachable under specified transformations, resources, policies and horizons?
Which distinctions must a representation preserve for specified inquiries or actions?
Which distinctions in realized transformation structure must remain recoverable?
When does relational information add explanatory or functional value beyond local properties?

packages.title: When history helps prediction
packages.question: In finite partially observed stochastic processes, when does recursively updated history recover predictive distinctions unavailable in current observation?
packages.cases: E0: present sufficient · E1: history disambiguates · E2: history is future-irrelevant
packages.limit: Does not establish universal or fundamental memory, or full-history retention.

packages.title: From local to global preservation
packages.question: When do local continuation and preservation judgments support a global judgment?
packages.cases: Transitive chain · monotonic drift · out-and-back loop · critical jump
packages.limit: Does not establish a metaphysical identity theory.

packages.title: Branching lineages
packages.question: Which distinctions are required for continuation claims under copying, branching and merging?
packages.cases: Linear succession · copy · symmetric fork · independent duplicate · merge
packages.limit: Current-state equivalence does not determine lineage relations. Human intuition is not ground truth.

packages.title: Constraints and viable futures
packages.question: Can targeted restrictions steer horizon-limited decisions away from states with fewer viable future targets?
packages.cases: Unnecessary restriction · correct protective restriction · harmful over-restriction
packages.limit: Removing edges does not expand raw structural reachability. Any benefit is conditional.
